elements.id-string-79: We assume that arbitration between the reader and writer for the shared memory is facilitated by Read-Copy-Update (RCU) mechanism.
elements.id-string-80: RCU is a lock-less concurrency construct that allows concurrent forward progress for both reader and writer.
elements.id-string-82: RCU can be broadly described in two steps \cite{kernelRCU}:
elements.id-string-83: To publish a newer version of a data item,the writer creates a copy of the RCU protected data item, modifies this copy with the newer version of this data item, and atomically replaces the old reference with a reference to this newer version.This publishing process runs concurrentlywith ongoing read processes that continue to read the old copy/version using the old reference.

elements.id-string-85: \textit{Remark 2: } RCU read operations can be performed concurrently without any locks, allowing for high concurrency and low contention.

elements.id-string-97: When the DP reader's inter-sample times form a renewal process, this is an example of the model of renewal process sampling of updates introduced in \cite{Yates-IT2020}.
elements.id-string-98: In this model, the DP reader generates  an age process $\dpage(t)$  at the input to the DP that is a sampled version of the max-age process $\maxage(t)$ in the memory.
elements.id-string-99: Specifically, in the absence of a read, $\dpage(t)$ continues to grow at unit rate.
elements.id-string-100: However, if the DP reader makes a read at time $\tau$, then $\dpage(t)$ is reset to $\dpage(\tau)=\maxage(\tau)$.
elements.id-string-101: This update pair is then processed by the DP  for a time $T$ so that at time $\tau+T$ a decision update with age $\dpage(\tau)+T$ is delivered to the monitor.
elements.id-string-102: The age at the monitor, $\monage(t)$,  is  then reduced to $\monage(\tau+T)=\maxage(\tau)+T$.
elements.id-string-103: At this time, the DP reader may choose to fetch a new sample pair from the memory, or it may choose to wait for a time $W$ before fetching the next sample pair.
elements.id-string-104: When the DP reader employs non-zero waiting times, we say the DP is using a {\em lazy sampling} policy \cite{Yates-isit2015}.
